ownershipNotes: session_open returns a Session that must be freed with session_close_buggy; internal allocations for name, cached_route, request_context are also owned by Session.
build_retry_batch returns a NULL-terminated array of strings; caller must free each string and the array. If fail_index is used, intermediate allocations are leaked.
queue_fanout_clone returns a heap copy of the payload; caller must free it. Bug: returns NULL after allocation if subscriber_enabled is 0, leaking the clone.
consume_batch frees each non-NULL string and the batch array itself.
queue_destroy_buggy only frees the head node and its payload, leaking remaining nodes.
session_close_buggy frees name and cached_route but misses request_context, causing a leak.
session_rename and session_replace_route allocate new strings and store them, leaking the previous values.
register_hook_context allocates a HookContext; if validator rejects, it returns without freeing the context, causing a leak.
explanation: Identify project-specific allocation/deallocation functions: session_open, build_retry_batch, queue_fanout_clone as allocators returning owned memory; consume_batch, queue_destroy_buggy, session_close_buggy as deallocators freeing owned memory. Internal static helpers (consume_batch) included. Several ownership bugs noted: missing frees, leaky early returns, incomplete destructors. Confidence high but not 100% due to possible oversight of internal allocation patterns.
